Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Expectation2: Ensure the safe and punctual operation of the subway train.
Situation2: A critical alert for a brake system malfunction has just appeared, requiring an immediate report and stop.
Story: The train rumbled beneath my feet, the familiar rhythm usually calming, but today my phone buzzed insistently in my pocket. Glancing at the screen, I saw it was Jamie. I hesitated, but answered, hearing their shaky voice, “Can you talk? I really need you right now.” I could hear the tears, the desperation. My mind raced—Jamie always counted on me to listen, to help them sort through the mess. I wanted to be there, to offer comfort, to be the friend they expected. But just as I opened my mouth, a shrill alarm blared from the control panel. A red light flashed: brake system malfunction. My training kicked in—protocol demanded I report and stop the train immediately, for everyone’s safety. My heart pounded. Jamie’s voice trembled in my ear, pleading for support, while the passengers behind me trusted me to keep them safe. I felt torn in two, caught between the urgent needs of a friend and the critical responsibility of my job, both demanding my full attention at the exact same moment.
